scope: arithmetic and timer-domain comparison; no physical clock, gap measurement, sleep or realtime guarantee

contract.low32: caller-declared elapsed upper bound from last accepted sample, strictly below 2^32 ticks; raw delta cannot verify declaration
contract.assumed: if bound unknown, assume fewer than one counter revolution; mark quality assumed until a new logical domain
contract.native64: same source epoch and rate, raw never wraps or resets; backward samples refuse without updating output
contract.fraction: carry fractional microseconds inside the same rate; variable rate stores numerator/rate, fixed 6MHz stores ticks/6
contract.known_pause: caller supplies integral microseconds since last accepted sample; same rate preserves fraction; changed rate requires explicit permission to discard nonzero fraction
contract.unknown_pause: explicit new logical epoch and caller-chosen anchor; no claim about unobserved elapsed duration
contract.outputs: unsuccessful begin/observe/resume preserves output and drop report; diagnostic history is not current time
contract.epoch: nonzero object-local generation, refuse wrap; source epoch and logical epoch are distinct
contract.concurrency: serialized, one clock object domain per timer client; no cross-object or cross-core identity guarantee

timer_adapter.observation_gap_us: strictly below 2^31; checked using accepted uint64 stamp
timer_adapter.quality: compare strict rejection versus explicit acceptance of assumed/rounded stamps
timer_adapter.domain_change_or_invalid_gap: stop future schedule, retain already pending notification with its old epoch
timer_adapter.delivery: explicit poll and take only, no callback or hidden work

unverified: source gap bounds and stable epoch/rate must be established externally
hardware frequency and calibration, debug halt and stalls
V006 and other series sleep retention and wakeup conditions
IRQ/core sharing and physical counter adaptation
timer/mailbox lifecycle integration and API adoption
